title: Concerto grosso in G minor, Op. 6 No. 8, “Christmas Concerto”
hook: Made “for the night of Christmas” in Rome, six short movements that end in a gentle pastorale, the music of shepherds’ pipes.

painting.title: The Holy Night (Adoration of the Shepherds)
painting.pairingNote: The shepherds crowd in out of the dark, and the only light comes from the newborn Child; the night of Christmas that Corelli’s concerto was “made for”, ending in the shepherds’ own music.

facts: Arcangelo Corelli was the most famous violinist in Rome, and his music was copied and admired all over Europe. His twelve concerti grossi, Op. 6, were probably written in the 1680s; he prepared them for print late in life, but they appeared in Amsterdam in 1714, a year after his death, dedicated to the Elector Palatine, Johann Wilhelm.

A [[concerto-grosso|concerto grosso]] sets a small group of soloists against the full string band. Here the soloists, the concertino, are two violins and a cello; the band, the ripieno, can be as large as the occasion allows. Sometimes they play together, sometimes the small group answers the large one, like an echo.

The score of No. 8 is headed *Fatto per la notte di Natale*, “made for the night of Christmas”. Corelli lived and worked for years in the palace of his patron Cardinal Pietro Ottoboni. He is recorded as playing a Christmas concerto for the cardinal in 1690, and the work is traditionally linked with Christmas Eve at Ottoboni’s palace.

The last movement, the [[pastorale|pastorale]], is marked *ad libitum*: it could be left out when the concerto was not played at Christmas. It imitates the *pifferari*, the bagpipe and reed-pipe players whose music belonged to Christmas in Italy: a sweet tune in pairs over a long-held bass. Handel took up the same idea in the *Pifa* of *Messiah*, and his own Op. 6 concerti grossi (1739) were modelled on Corelli’s.
bigPicture.inOneLine: a solemn opening (I), a quick chase (II), a tender song (III), two quick dances (IV–V), a shepherds’ pastorale (VI).

movements.heading: Vivace – Grave
movements.summary: A few bars of quick, firm chords, then a long, slow Grave. In the Grave the strings hold their notes and lean into clashes that slowly resolve, one after another. Corelli marked it *Arcate, sostenuto e come stà*: bowed, sustained and played as written, without added ornaments.

mainIdeas.name: The Vivace
mainIdeas.description: a short burst of chords for everyone.

mainIdeas.name: The Grave
mainIdeas.description: long, held notes that rub against each other and then resolve, in a slow chain.

stops.hear: A few quick, firm chords from the whole band
stops.happening: The Vivace, like a call to attention

stops.hear: Everything slows; long, bowed notes that clash gently and then settle
stops.happening: The Grave: a chain of suspensions

stops.hear: The clashes grow richer as more voices join the chain
stops.happening: The Grave moves through related keys

stops.label: Last 15 seconds
stops.hear: A slow close on a chord that leaves the music open

notice: In the Grave, listen for the moment of tension when one note is held over against the next chord, and the small release when it moves down.

notes.title: In this recording
notes.body: The English Concert play on period instruments; Trevor Pinnock directs from the harpsichord, with Simon Standage and Micaela Comberti (violins) and Jaap ter Linden (cello) as the concertino. The recording was made in London in April 1987 for the complete set of twelve. On the Spotify album this concerto is tracks 36–41.

movements.heading: Allegro
movements.summary: A quick movement in which the two solo violins chase each other, one copying the other a moment later, over a busy bass. The full band joins in to drive the music on.

mainIdeas.name: The chase
mainIdeas.description: a quick figure in one violin, taken up at once by the other.

stops.hear: Quick, lively lines over a busy bass; one violin starts and the other follows close behind
stops.happening: Imitation between the two solo violins

stops.hear: The whole band takes over, fuller and louder
The two violins alone again, trading phrases

stops.label: Last 20 seconds
stops.hear: Everyone together for a firm close in G minor

notice: Follow the two violins. Their lines cross and overlap so closely that it is hard to tell which one is leading.

movements.heading: Adagio – Allegro – Adagio
movements.summary: The heart of the concerto, in a warm E-flat major. The two violins sing a slow, tender duet over a quietly pulsing bass. A quicker middle section brings more movement and some unrest, and then the slow duet returns.

mainIdeas.name: The duet
mainIdeas.description: two violins singing close together, often in thirds, over soft, even steps in the bass.

mainIdeas.name: The middle section
mainIdeas.description: quicker, with busy figures in the violins.

stops.hear: Two violins sing a slow, tender duet over a soft, walking bass
The pace quickens; busy, running figures pass between the violins
The slow duet returns

stops.label: Last 20 seconds
stops.hear: A soft, warm close

notice: In the slow sections, listen to how the two violins move together, the same shape a few notes apart, like two singers in harmony.

movements.heading: Vivace
movements.summary: A short, quick dance in three, crisp and bright, almost like a minuet taken at speed. Each half is played twice.

mainIdeas.name: The dance
mainIdeas.description: a quick tune in three for everyone, with firm chords on the beat.

stops.hear: A crisp, quick dance in three
stops.happening: The first half, then its repeat

stops.hear: The tune moves on to new keys
stops.happening: The second half, then its repeat

stops.label: Last 5 seconds
stops.hear: A quick, firm end

notice: Notice how short it is: about a minute. Corelli’s movements are compact, and the concerto lives from their contrasts.

movements.heading: Allegro
movements.summary: A lively finale in quick two-time, in which the solo violins run in fast figures and the band answers with strong, short phrases. It closes in G minor, and the Pastorale that follows will change everything to major.

mainIdeas.name: The running figures
mainIdeas.description: quick notes in the solo violins, tossed back and forth.

stops.hear: A lively tune for everyone, in quick twos
The solo violins race in quick, running notes; the band answers in short bursts
The music builds, the exchanges coming faster

stops.label: Last 15 seconds
stops.hear: A firm, final cadence in G minor
stops.happening: The end of the minor-key concerto

notice: Listen to the last chord in G minor. The next movement starts in G major, the same note at the bottom, but a different, brighter world.

movements.heading: Pastorale: Largo
movements.summary: The Christmas music proper. The key turns to G major and the rhythm to a gentle rocking in twelve slow beats to the bar. Over a long-held bass, like the drone of a bagpipe, the violins play a sweet tune in pairs, as the *pifferari* did on their pipes. At the end the music slows and fades away.

mainIdeas.name: The pastorale tune
mainIdeas.description: a gently rocking melody in two violins, moving together in thirds.

mainIdeas.name: The drone
mainIdeas.description: long, held notes in the bass, like a bagpipe.

stops.hear: The music turns bright and gentle; a rocking tune in two violins over a long-held bass note
stops.happening: The [[pastorale|pastorale]] begins, in G major, over a [[drone|drone]]

stops.hear: The two solo violins answer the band on their own, softer
The tune moves to a new key; the held bass moves with it
stops.happening: A brief journey away from G major

stops.hear: The rocking tune back in G major

stops.label: Last 40 seconds
stops.hear: The music slows and grows quieter, ending on long, soft chords

notice: Listen to the lowest notes. For long stretches they do not move at all, just as a bagpipe’s drone does not.
Compare the start of this movement with the end of the last one. The key has turned from minor to major.

threads.title: Small group, large band
threads.body: In every movement the concertino of two violins and a cello sets off against the full ripieno, sometimes leading, sometimes echoing.

threads.title: Two violins as one voice
threads.body: Again and again the two solo violins move together a third apart, in the tender Adagio and in the Pastorale.

threads.title: From church to Christmas
threads.body: The concerto follows the pattern of a church concerto, slow and fast movements in turn, and the optional Pastorale turns it into music for one night of the year.
